title: Three-layer idempotency for Peer/deliver is correct and should be defended
description: The sender_msg_id idempotency guarantee is enforced at three independent layers: (1) application-level find_by_sender_msg_id check before insert, (2) UNIQUE INDEX on (chat_id, sender_msg_id) in the DB, (3) BEFORE INSERT trigger aborting NULL sender_msg_id. Each layer catches a failure mode the others don't: (1) catches retransmissions before they hit the DB, (2) catches concurrent delivery attempts that race past (1), (3) catches future code changes that accidentally pass NULL. A future contributor might suggest 'simplifying' to just the UNIQUE INDEX. That would be wrong: (1) is needed to avoid the DB constraint error path in normal operation, (3) is needed because SQLite UNIQUE INDEX permits multiple NULLs (so a NULL sender_msg_id would silently bypass the dedup guarantee).
